key_insight: SAGE is an agentic system that converts a user-specified embodied task into a realistic, simulator-ready 3D scene by understanding intent and autonomously constructing physically valid environments. It scales scene generation beyond brittle rule-based pipelines by iteratively planning, placing, and validating objects.
problem_solved: Reduces the cost, safety risks, and manual effort of collecting real-world embodied-agent data by producing scalable, realistic, and physically valid 3D simulation environments that are ready for downstream embodied tasks.
method: Task understanding: parse user-specified embodied tasks (e.g., 'pick up a bowl and place it on the table') to derive goals and constraints.
Agentic scene synthesis: use iterative agent modules to plan object selection, placement, and scene layout while enforcing task affordances.
Physics-aware validation & export: validate scene stability and interactions with a physics check, then export simulator-ready assets and annotations.
impact: Enables practitioners to rapidly generate high-quality synthetic environments for training and evaluating embodied agents, improving safety, reproducibility, and dataset diversity while reducing manual scene engineering.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: user task → intent parser → agentic planner → scene builder → physics validator → simulator export
